headline.en: Pollen Robotics publishes the Microduck 3D model files under a Creative Commons licence they write as 'BY-SA-NC' with NO version number; canonically that is CC BY-NC-SA. Their code is Apache 2.0. Their press kit says the hardware is not open source. On the plain reading of CC BY-NC-SA, geometry taken from those files may be reproduced and built for NON-commercial purposes only, and anything derived from it that is shared must carry the same licence. SELLING units made from that geometry is NOT permitted by the published licence, at any quantity. TWO THINGS ARE DIFFERENT AND A FACTORY SHOULD KNOW BOTH. First, one board IS fully open: Pollen publish the RPI Robot HAT under Apache-2.0 with KiCad source, Gerbers, BOM, pick-and-place and STEP — it may be manufactured and sold commercially. Second, Pollen's terms of sale forbid a buyer from dismantling or reverse engineering a purchased robot, so nobody on this project should buy one and open it; we never have. A commercial licence from Pollen, or a counsel opinion that the manufactured parts are not 'Adapted Material' of a copyright work, is what would change the answer on the robot. Neither exists as of 2026-09-04. CURRENCY, so a factory knows how old this page is: every fact was re-measured on 2026-09-04, the two Pollen READMEs came back byte-identical to the copies archived the night before, and upstream's develop branch is still sitting on the exact commit our geometry was taken from (29e887e) — zero commits of drift between the licence reading and this pack.
headline.zh: Pollen Robotics 以其写作 'BY-SA-NC'、未注明版本号的知识共享许可证发布 Microduck 3D 模型文件；其规范名称为 CC BY-NC-SA。其代码为 Apache 2.0。其新闻资料说明硬件不是开源的。按 CC BY-NC-SA 的字面含义，取自这些文件的几何体只能用于非商业目的的复制与制作，任何由此派生并分享的内容必须采用相同许可证。以该几何体制造的整机，无论数量多少，均不允许销售。有两点不同，工厂必须知道。第一，有一块电路板确为完全开源：Pollen 以 Apache-2.0 公布 RPI Robot HAT，含 KiCad 源文件、Gerber、BOM、贴片坐标与 STEP——可以商业制造与销售。第二，Pollen 的销售条款禁止买方拆解或逆向工程所购机器人，因此本项目任何人都不应购买并拆解；我们从未这样做过。就整机而言，能改变结论的只有 Pollen 出具的商业许可，或律师认定所制造零件不属于受版权保护作品的'演绎材料'的意见书。截至 2026-09-04，两者均不存在。时效性说明（供工厂判断本页新旧）：全部事实已于 2026-09-04 重新实测；Pollen 的两份 README 重新下载后与前一晚存档的字节完全一致；上游 develop 分支仍停在我方几何数据的来源提交（29e887e）——从读取许可证到本资料包交付，上游零提交漂移。

reading: Pollen has said in writing, twice, that the mechanical and electronic design is not open. The CC-licensed STLs are simulation assets exported from their Onshape CAD (SOURCE-COMMIT.txt: 'exported from Onshape by onshape-to-robot'), not a release of the manufacturing design.

QUALIFIED 2026-09-04 by F11: the sentence is true of the MECHANICAL files and of the Microduck-specific boards, but it is NOT true of every electronic design file. Pollen has published one complete, manufacturable board — the RPI Robot HAT — under Apache-2.0, with KiCad source, Gerbers, BOM, pick-and-place and STEP. The press-kit fact sheet's own wording is narrower than the web page's and survives this: it says the design files are 'not covered by that statement', not that no design file exists in the open.
No BOM, no STEP, no PCB files, no Onshape link for the Microduck MECHANICS has been published (research/01-product-and-specs.md:335).

NONE of our geometry comes from Open Duck Mini. Every mesh on our shelf is mapped to pollen-robotics/microduck_rl assets (spec/mesh-to-part.json). Open Duck Mini's licence therefore does not govern our parts; it is context, not a source.

Nothing in the licence is a volume threshold, a royalty schedule or a per-unit fee; NC is a purpose test.

The product's appearance was first disclosed publicly on 2026-08-27 (press kit, The Register). questions.q_en: May we manufacture units from geometry derived from these assets?
questions.q_zh: 我们可以用源自这些资产的几何体制造整机吗？
questions.verdict: PASS for non-commercial engineering units; PASS without limit for the Robot HAT board; FAIL for production units intended for sale
questions.plain_reading: CC 2(a)(1)(b) grants the right to 'produce, reproduce, and Share Adapted Material for NonCommercial purposes only'. Building prototype and validation units for our own engineering, not sold, not offered, is within the grant provided attribution (3(a)) is kept on anything shared. A production run whose purpose is sale is 'primarily intended for or directed towards commercial advantage' (1(k)) and is outside the grant. ONE EXCEPTION, MEASURED 2026-09-04 (F11): the RPI Robot HAT board is published by Pollen under Apache-2.0 with its complete production package. Boards made from those files may be manufactured, modified and sold, in any quantity, subject only to Apache-2.0's notice conditions and to not using Pollen's name on them.
questions.what_the_factory_may_do_now: Print, machine and assemble engineering units from our drawings for test and validation; keep Pollen's attribution on every file; share nothing derived from the meshes outside the project except under BY-NC-SA. Fabricate and populate the RPI Robot HAT from Pollen's own Gerbers, BOM and pick-and-place file with no quantity limit (F11).
questions.what_the_factory_may_not_do_now: Cut production tooling (moulds) whose purpose is units for sale, on the strength of this licence alone. Do not buy a retail Microduck and take it apart to measure it: Pollen's terms of sale forbid dismantling and reverse engineering by the buyer, and forbid resale without a distribution contract (F14). No unit has been bought or opened by this project, and that clean position is worth keeping until Q-E is answered.
questions.settles_it: Q-A (a licence from Pollen) or Q-B (counsel: the parts are not Adapted Material of a copyright work).

questions.q_zh: 我们可以销售这些整机吗？
questions.verdict: FAIL on the published licence, for anything carrying the geometry; PASS for the Robot HAT board alone
questions.plain_reading: Selling a unit is monetary compensation for an object produced from the Licensed Material. 2(a)(1) limits every licensed right to NonCommercial purposes. There is no clause that permits sale, and 6(a) terminates the licence automatically on breach. Pollen has also said the hardware is not open (F4) and sells the same product at USD 399.00 (F8). The Robot HAT board is the one part of the machine that is separately, commercially licensed (Apache-2.0, F11) and could be sold on its own. Selling the ROBOT is what fails.
questions.settles_it: Q-A or Q-B. Nothing we can do inside the repository changes this answer.

questions.q_en: May we sell commercially at volume, given the non-commercial clause?
questions.q_zh: 鉴于非商业条款，我们可以大批量商业销售吗？
questions.verdict: FAIL on the published licence — volume does not change it
questions.plain_reading: The NC clause (1(k)) is a purpose test with no quantity threshold: one unit sold and ten thousand units sold are both 'directed towards commercial advantage'. CC's FAQ says whether a use is commercial 'will depend on the specifics of the situation and the intentions of the user'; the intention here — a factory, tooling, a price list — is commercial on its face. Two further gates sit on the same sale and are independent of the copyright answer: Pollen's legal notice forbids use of their name and logo without written agreement (F13), and the EU unregistered Community design right that arose on first disclosure, 2026-08-27, runs three years against COPYING the appearance (F9). A trademark search run tonight found no MICRODUCK mark indexed anywhere in TMview, with a working control — that is a measurement, not a clearance (F15).
questions.settles_it: Q-A or Q-B. Note that Q-B, if it lands in our favour, answers only copyright; F9 (trade names, unregistered EU design right from 2026-08-27, any registered designs or patents) is a separate gate on the same sale.
